title: Can a Parent Without Custody Still Get Visitation?
desc: A parent who does not get custody in Uttarakhand can still ask the Family Court for visitation under section 12 of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890.
why: Courts across India keep deciding how much access a parent without custody should get, and parents in Haldwani and Nainital often don't know that custody and visitation are two separate questions.
keyPoints: Losing custody does not end a parent's right to ask for visitation; courts treat the two as separate questions.
Section 12 of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 lets a court pass a temporary order for a minor's custody or access while the main case is pending.
Visitation can be supervised, limited to daytime, or expanded over time, based only on the child's welfare.
A visitation order can be changed later if circumstances change, so it is not the final word.

sections.h: Can a parent get visitation without having custody?
p: Yes. A parent who does not have custody of a child can still ask a Family Court for visitation rights, since custody and visitation are decided as separate questions under Indian law. Section 12 of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 lets the court pass a temporary order for the custody or protection of a minor while a guardianship case is still pending. Family Courts, including the one at Haldwani, use this power to fix regular access for the parent who does not have custody.

The same principle applies when custody is decided inside a divorce case. Section 26 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 lets the court pass orders on a child's custody, maintenance and education at any stage of the proceedings, and change them later.

sections.h: What kind of visitation does a court usually order?
p: There is no fixed formula. Courts have ordered anything from short supervised meetings to overnight stays, depending on the child's age, comfort with the parent, and any history of conflict or violence. Some orders start with daytime access only and move to overnight stays once the child settles in.

If one parent has broken an earlier order, for example by not returning the child on time, a court can cut back visitation or require it to be supervised. The child's welfare, not either parent's convenience, decides the outcome every time.

sections.h: Can a visitation order be changed later?
p: A visitation order is not permanent. Either parent can go back to the same court and ask for a change if the child's needs, school timing, or either parent's circumstances change. Courts expect parents to keep following the existing order until a new one is passed, even if they disagree with it.

whatToDo: Ask for interim visitation at the very first hearing, rather than waiting for the custody case to end.
Keep a written record of missed or denied visits; it helps if you later need to go back to court.
If safety is a concern, ask the court for supervised visitation rather than avoiding the issue.
Follow the current order exactly, even an interim one, while you apply to change it.

hi.title: क्या कस्टडी न मिलने पर भी बच्चे से मिलने का अधिकार मिल सकता है?
keyPoints: कस्टडी न मिलने से मिलने (विजिटेशन) का अधिकार खत्म नहीं होता, अदालत दोनों को अलग-अलग तय करती है।
गार्जियंस एंड वार्ड्स एक्ट, 1890 की धारा 12 के तहत अदालत मामला लंबित रहते हुए अस्थायी आदेश दे सकती है।
मिलने की व्यवस्था निगरानी में, सीमित समय के लिए, या बाद में बढ़ाकर दी जा सकती है, बच्चे के हित के अनुसार।
यह आदेश स्थायी नहीं है, हालात बदलने पर दोबारा अदालत से बदलवाया जा सकता है।
p: हल्द्वानी की फैमिली कोर्ट सहित सभी अदालतें यह ध्यान रखती हैं कि बच्चे का भला किसमें है, न कि किस माता-पिता को ज़्यादा सुविधा चाहिए।

sources.title: Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, section 12 (Indian Kanoon)
